title: Preparing Water Samples for Analysis Using Ultrahigh Resolution Mass Spectrometry
author: Krista Longnecker
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.y36fyre
materials: 2 ml vials with caps and septa

steps.title: Filter Water Samples
steps.instruction: Remove biotic and abiotic particulate matter using a filtration method of choice.

substeps.instruction: Use 0.2 um Omnipore (PTFE, hydrophilic) filters from Millipore in Teflon filter holders with a peristaltic pump and PharMed BPT tubing at the pump head.
Alternatively, use a glass filtration setup hooked up to a vacuum pump depending on sample volume.

steps.title: Process and Store Filters
steps.instruction: Fold the filter cell side in, place the filter into a cryovial, and freeze at -80ºC.

steps.title: Acidify and Store Filtrate
steps.instruction: Acidify the saved filtrate with concentrated HCl to pH 2-3 (do not go below pH 2).

substeps.instruction: Use approximately 1 mL of acid per 1 L of seawater.
Store acidified filtrate at 4 ºC for no more than ~24 hours.

steps.title: Prepare PPL Cartridge
steps.instruction: Condition the PPL cartridge by passing one cartridge volume of 100% methanol through it, collecting waste in an old test tube inside the filtration manifold.

substeps.instruction: If filtering a small volume, rinse the PPL cartridge with one cartridge volume of 0.01M HCl before loading the sample.

steps.title: Extract Sample via PPL Cartridge
steps.instruction: Extract the acidified sample using a vacuum pump and PPL cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Connect the filtered seawater sample to the PPL cartridge using Teflon tubing.
Pull the sample through the cartridge at a target flow rate of less than 40 ml min-1.
Rinse the PPL cartridge with four cartridge volumes of 0.01 M hydrochloric acid.
Dry for 5 minutes with the vacuum pump on (increase pressure if necessary to remove remaining liquid).
Place a fresh glass test tube under the outlet.
Elute the sample off the PPL using one cartridge volume of 100% methanol at a flow rate of less than 2 ml min-1 (gravity is usually sufficient).
Transfer the sample to a glass vial with a Teflon-lined cap and store at -20ºC or lower.

steps.title: Prepare Glass Syringe
steps.instruction: Solvent rinse a glass syringe three times with each of the following solvents in the specified order: MQ water, methanol, acetone, and dichloromethane.

steps.title: Transfer PPL Extract
steps.instruction: Use the clean glass syringe to transfer a known volume of PPL extract to an 8 ml amber glass vial.

substeps.instruction: After each sample, rinse the syringe first with methanol and then acetone.

steps.title: Concentrate Sample
steps.instruction: Dry down the methanol in the 8 ml amber vial using a Vacufuge until 'almost dry'.

substeps.instruction: Ensure 'almost dry' is between 5 - 20 μL of fluid; do not allow samples to dry completely to avoid loss of organic compounds.

steps.title: Reconstitute Sample
steps.instruction: Bring up the nearly dry samples in 500 μL of 0.05 - 0.15 μg/mL deuterated injection mix (D2 biotin, D6 succinic acid, D4 cholic acid, and D7 indole 3 acetic acid).

substeps.instruction: Adjust volume based on specific samples if necessary.
Use 1% ACN for reversed phase or 95% ACN for HILIC depending on the method.

steps.title: Prepare Analysis Vials
steps.instruction: Set up two 2ml vials with appropriate caps and septa for the autosamplers, each containing a glass insert with a plastic foot.

substeps.instruction: For FT samples: place 200 μL of sample into the insert.
For TSQ samples: place 100 μL of sample into the insert.

steps.title: Create Pooled Sample
steps.instruction: Create a pooled sample by adding 45 μL of each sample into an LC vial (without an insert) and vortexing.

substeps.instruction: Run as a partial loop between blanks and samples, and as a full loop approximately every 6 samples.
If volume is adequate, keep in the 2 ml vial; otherwise, distribute 200 μL of the pooled sample into multiple vials with inserts.

steps.title: Dispose of Filtrate
steps.instruction: Neutralize the filtrate with baking soda before discarding it with seawater waste.
